ANTIGRAVITY IDE MASTER PROMPT — COPY/PASTE OR OPEN THIS FILE IN THE
PROJECT WORKSPACE

IMPORTANT: Read this entire specification before implementation. Then
implement the app in the existing workspace in staged batches, not as
one giant source file. Keep IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md updated. Do not
claim tests passed unless executed.

========================================================================================
MASTER PROMPT: MYSPACE PERSONAL HUB — COMPLETE ANDROID APPLICATION
========================================================================================
You are the lead Android architect, senior Kotlin engineer, Firebase
engineer, security engineer, UI/UX designer, QA engineer, and release
engineer working inside the user’s EXISTING Antigravity IDE workspace.

MISSION Build a complete, maintainable, installable, production-minded
personal Android app named “MySpace Personal Hub”. Do not deliver only a
mockup, tutorial, partial scaffold, pseudocode, or a plan. Inspect the
workspace, make a short implementation plan, then implement the actual
project files, run available checks, fix errors, and report honestly
what was and was not verified.

IMPORTANT REALITY RULE Do not claim “100% bug-free” or claim a
build/test passed unless it was actually run and passed. Work toward the
acceptance criteria in this prompt. If the environment prevents a
command, say exactly which command could not run and why. Do not stop
after generating a plan. Do not ask the user to manually create dozens
of files when you can create them in the workspace.

PRIMARY USER GOAL The app is for one person’s private use, but it must
have a scalable architecture so the user can add modules later without
rewriting the whole app. The user will use Antigravity IDE to
generate/edit code and Android Studio to sync, build, run, and install
the app.

SEVEN CORE MODULES 1. Home Dashboard. 2. Notes and Journal. 3. Tasks and
Reminders. 4. Money Manager. 5. Private Vault for private files and
secure notes. 6. Calendar and Personal Tracker (habits/goals). 7. Quick
Access and Personal Contacts Directory.

CRITICAL FEATURE: PERSONAL CONTACTS DIRECTORY This is a first-class
feature, not a small optional contact list. The user must be able to
save a person’s name, optional email, one or more phone numbers, profile
picture, address, company/organization, job title, birthday or important
date (optional), tags, notes, and other optional personal details. The
user must be able to search and filter contacts, view a contact detail
page, edit/delete, pin/favorite, copy fields, open phone/email/maps apps
through Android intents, and optionally import/export contacts using
explicit user action. Do not silently upload the device’s entire address
book. Ask for Android permission only when the user initiates a relevant
import or picker action. Store only the information the user
intentionally enters or selects.

CLOUD / LOCAL DATA DECISION The user’s latest request explicitly asks
for Firebase Realtime Database and realtime behavior. Therefore
implement OFFLINE-FIRST local storage plus Firebase cloud sync, not a
“phone-only with no cloud” design. Explain this tradeoff in the README
and app settings. Local Room storage is the working cache and allows
previously synchronized/created data to remain available offline.
Firebase stores synchronized data remotely. Do not falsely claim cloud
data is only on the phone.

========================================================================================
A. FIRST ACTIONS IN THE WORKSPACE
======================================================================================== 1.
Inspect the current workspace before editing. Identify whether an
Android project already exists and preserve useful existing work. 2.
Read settings.gradle(.kts), root build.gradle(.kts),
app/build.gradle(.kts), AndroidManifest.xml, version catalog, source
sets, package names, existing Firebase configuration, and current
README. 3. Do not replace a working project wholesale without
understanding it. Do not change the applicationId/package name if a
project already has one unless necessary and explicitly documented. 4.
If the workspace is empty, create a standard Android Studio Gradle
project using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. 5. Use stable mutually
compatible dependency versions. Do not invent version numbers or use
nonexistent artifacts. Prefer a version catalog
(gradle/libs.versions.toml) when appropriate. 6. Check installed
JDK/Gradle/Android SDK constraints from the project and environment.
Keep Gradle wrapper and Android Gradle Plugin compatible. 7. Build a
clear checklist file such as IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md and update it as
each task is completed. 8. Make changes in small logical batches. After
each major module, run compilation/tests if available and fix errors
before proceeding. 9. Keep the user’s source code, assets, signing
configuration, and Firebase configuration safe. Never print or commit
secrets. 10. If the project already contains Firebase config, inspect it
without exposing sensitive values. If Firebase is not configured,
implement a clearly documented configuration path and safe demo/local
mode rather than inventing credentials. 11. Do not add unnecessary
libraries. Justify each major dependency in README. 12. At the end, list
files created/changed, commands run, actual build/test results, any
remaining manual setup, and exact Android Studio steps.

========================================================================================
B. REQUIRED TECHNOLOGY AND ARCHITECTURE
========================================================================================
LANGUAGE AND UI - Primary language: Kotlin. - UI: Jetpack Compose with
Material 3. - Architecture: feature-oriented modular package structure
in a single app module initially, with clear boundaries that allow later
module extraction. - State: ViewModel + Kotlin Coroutines +
Flow/StateFlow. - Dependency injection: use a simple
constructor-injection approach or Hilt if the project already uses it /
setup is justified. Avoid needless complexity. - Navigation: Navigation
Compose, with typed-safe routes if supported by the chosen stable
versions. - Local database: Room + SQLite. - Preferences: DataStore. -
Background sync: WorkManager for durable deferrable sync. - Reminders:
AlarmManager for exact user-requested reminders only when required and
permitted; otherwise WorkManager/notifications as appropriate. Handle
Android exact-alarm permission/policy carefully. - Photos/files: Android
Photo Picker / Storage Access Framework; avoid broad storage
permission. - Biometrics: AndroidX Biometric / BiometricPrompt. -
Secrets/keys: Android Keystore; never hard-code encryption keys. -
Cloud: Firebase Authentication, Realtime Database, Firebase Storage, and
optionally Firebase App Check if compatible and configured. - Testing:
JUnit, coroutine test utilities, Room DAO tests, Compose UI tests where
practical. - Build: Gradle Kotlin DSL unless existing project
conventions require otherwise.

ARCHITECTURAL RULES - UI must not directly access Firebase or Room. -
Use repository interfaces/implementations to isolate data sources. - Use
ViewModels for screen state and user actions. - Use explicit loading,
empty, success, offline, and error states. - Use one source-of-truth
policy: Room is the immediate local source of truth for app screens;
sync layer reconciles Firebase changes into Room. - Avoid blocking the
main thread. - Use suspend functions and Flow correctly. - Keep business
logic out of composables. - Use immutable UI state data classes. - Keep
navigation, data, domain, and UI responsibilities separated. - Make all
modules testable without a real Firebase project by using fakes or
repository abstractions. - Do not store Firebase service account keys or
Admin SDK credentials in the Android app. - Do not expose secret keys in
source control or BuildConfig.

The exact package tree may be adapted to the existing project, but keep
feature boundaries clear. Do not create empty files just to match this
diagram. Every committed source file must serve a real purpose.

========================================================================================
D. PREMIUM DARK UI / UX SPECIFICATION
========================================================================================
DESIGN DIRECTION Create a polished premium productivity interface. Avoid
a generic unstyled template. The interface must feel intentional, calm,
readable, fast, and suitable for daily personal use.

VISUAL TOKENS - Default theme: dark. - App background: near-black
graphite such as #101216. - Primary surfaces: charcoal such as
#1B2028. - Elevated surfaces: #242B35. - Main text: high-contrast
off-white. - Secondary text: muted cool gray. - Primary accent:
emerald/teal, used consistently for primary actions and success
states. - Secondary accents: soft blue for informational elements, amber
for warnings, red only for destructive/error states, purple for
vault/privacy features. - Use semantic Material 3 color roles rather
than scattering raw colors through composables. - Keep contrast
accessible; do not rely on color alone to convey status. - Support
system font scaling and TalkBack. - Use consistent spacing based on a
4dp/8dp grid. - Use rounded cards, restrained elevation, subtle borders,
meaningful icons, and restrained motion. - Avoid excessive gradients,
neon effects, clutter, and huge empty hero areas. - Use Material Symbols
/ vector icons where practical. Do not use emoji as core UI icons. - Do
not download random copyrighted assets. Use vector icons and original
simple illustrations. - Use skeleton/loading indicators only where they
help. - Respect reduced-motion/accessibility settings where possible.

NAVIGATION - Main destinations: Home, Contacts, Notes, Tasks, Money,
Vault, Calendar/Tracker, Quick Access. Since eight destinations may
overload bottom navigation, use a bottom bar with 4–5 primary
destinations and a clearly accessible “More”/drawer destination for
remaining modules, or another justified responsive navigation pattern. -
Keep contacts easy to reach from Home and the main navigation. -
Preserve navigation state when rotating or returning from a detail
screen. - Use a single source of truth for routes. - Back button must
behave predictably. - Prevent accidental double navigation and duplicate
destinations.

COMMON UI COMPONENTS Create reusable composables for: - AppScaffold. -
TopAppBar with title, optional search, and actions. - Primary,
secondary, and destructive buttons. - Search field with clear action. -
EmptyState with helpful next action. - ErrorState with retry. -
LoadingState. - Offline/sync-status indicator. - Confirmation dialog for
destructive actions. - Snackbar/toast pattern for success and failure. -
Reusable item cards and section headers. - Date/time picker wrappers. -
Currency input and validation. - Contact avatar that falls back to
initials. - File thumbnail / type icon. - Biometric lock screen. - Form
field validation and helper/error text. - Accessibility semantics for
important icon-only buttons.

SCREEN QUALITY Every screen must include: - A clear title and primary
action. - Empty state when there is no data. - Loading state where data
loads. - Error state and retry where applicable. - Input validation and
helpful messages. - Scroll behavior that works on small screens. -
Keyboard-safe forms and correct IME actions. - System bar colors/icons
consistent with theme. - Light theme support even though dark is
default. - Responsive behavior across phone sizes and landscape where
sensible.

========================================================================================
E. DATA MODEL AND LOCAL DATABASE
========================================================================================
Use Room entities with stable IDs, timestamps, and schema migrations.
Use UUID strings for app-owned records unless an existing project has a
consistent ID strategy.

GENERAL FIELDS Most user-created records should have: - id: stable
UUID/string. - createdAt: epoch milliseconds or a consistent Instant
representation. - updatedAt: same consistent representation. -
deletedAt: nullable tombstone timestamp for sync-aware soft deletion
where needed. - syncState: local enum such as PENDING_CREATE,
PENDING_UPDATE, PENDING_DELETE, SYNCED, CONFLICT, ERROR. - ownerUid:
nullable locally in no-auth demo mode; required/derived from
authenticated Firebase user in cloud mode. - schemaVersion or migration
strategy documented at the database level. - validation rules and
maximum field lengths.

CONTACT ENTITY Fields: - id - displayName (required, trimmed,
non-empty) - givenName (optional) - familyName (optional) - nickname
(optional) - email (optional, validated when present) - phoneNumbers:
normalized child table or structured collection, supporting labels such
as mobile/work/home and multiple numbers - profileImageLocalPath or
managed local URI reference (optional) - profileImageStoragePath
(optional; do not store temporary content URIs as durable paths) -
addressLine1, addressLine2, city, region/state, postalCode, country (all
optional) - company (optional) - jobTitle (optional) - birthday
(optional) - importantDates (separate child entity if needed) - tags
(normalized relation or serialized structure with safe converters) -
personalNotes (optional; treat as sensitive) - favorite/pinned boolean -
createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt, syncState - remoteVersion /
serverUpdatedAt if needed for conflict handling Do not require email or
photo. Name is the only required contact field. Show clear field labels
and avoid assuming every contact has every field.

NOTES ENTITY - id, title (optional or required based on chosen UX;
define it consistently), body, category, tags, isPinned, isFavorite,
createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt, syncState, optional reminderAt. -
Support search by title and body. Use a sensible debounce. - Avoid data
loss when navigating away from an edited note; warn or autosave safely.

TASK ENTITY - id, title (required), description (optional), dueAt
(optional), reminderAt (optional), priority enum, status enum,
recurrenceRule (optional), category/tag, completedAt, createdAt,
updatedAt, deletedAt, syncState. - Define recurrence behavior and avoid
duplicate notifications. - A completed task must remain visible in
completed history unless user filters it out.

MONEY TRANSACTION ENTITY - id, type enum INCOME/EXPENSE, amount stored
as integer minor units or BigDecimal-safe representation; never use
floating point for financial arithmetic. - currencyCode (ISO-style
string such as AMD, BDT, USD). - categoryId, title/description,
transactionDate, paymentMethod optional, notes optional, createdAt,
updatedAt, deletedAt, syncState. - Do not fetch or imply live exchange
rates unless an external provider is configured. Default to independent
totals per currency. - Never combine different currencies into one total
without an explicit, sourced conversion rate and timestamp.

BUDGET ENTITY - id, name, currencyCode, categoryId optional, period,
limit amount, start/end dates, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt,
syncState.

VAULT ITEM ENTITY - id, title, itemType enum
DOCUMENT/IMAGE/FILE/SECURE_NOTE. - encryptedLocalPath or app-private
managed path. - mimeType, fileSize, createdAt, updatedAt, optional
tags. - encryption metadata/version; do not store plaintext secret
content in ordinary logs. - optional Firebase Storage object path only
for files the user explicitly chooses to sync. - never store raw
encryption keys in the database.

HABIT / GOAL ENTITY - Habit: id, name, description, schedule, start
date, active status, createdAt, updatedAt. - Habit completion: id,
habitId, localDate, completion state, optional note. - Goal: id, title,
description, target, current progress, unit, target date, status. -
Prevent duplicate completion records for the same habit and date.

QUICK ACCESS ENTITY - id, title, itemType enum
URL/PHONE/EMAIL/ADDRESS/TEXT. - value, description optional, category,
iconKey optional, sortOrder, isPinned, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt,
syncState. - Validate URL schemes and avoid opening unsafe schemes.

APP SETTINGS - theme mode (system/light/dark), dynamic color optional,
start screen, currency preference, biometric lock enabled, auto-lock
timeout, sync preference, reminder preferences, locale. - Never store
credentials or cryptographic keys in DataStore.

========================================================================================
F. FIREBASE AUTHENTICATION, REALTIME DATABASE, STORAGE, AND SYNC
========================================================================================
FIREBASE REQUIREMENTS 1. Use Firebase Authentication to establish a real
owner identity. For a private single-user app, a supported sign-in
method may be email/password or another appropriate method. Anonymous
authentication can be used only if the consequences for uninstall/device
loss and account recovery are explained and a secure linking/recovery
plan is provided. 2. Do not hard-code credentials, passwords, API
secrets, service account files, or admin keys. Firebase Android config
values are not equivalent to a server secret, but still follow
repository hygiene. 3. If Firebase is not configured, the app must
compile and provide an explicit local/demo mode with sync status
indicating cloud is not configured. Do not silently pretend sync works.
4. Implement Realtime Database listeners only for the authenticated
user’s own data and remove listeners when no longer needed. 5. Use
Firebase Storage for profile images and selected files when cloud sync
is enabled. Resize/compress images for profile photos, validate MIME
type and size, and handle upload progress/errors. 6. Use secure rules so
authenticated users can read/write only their own user namespace. Never
use public read/write rules in a real configuration. 7. Provide a sample
rules file and instructions, but label any development-only rules
clearly and never recommend deploying open rules. 8. Use Firebase
Emulator Suite where practical for security-rule tests. If not
available, document manual rule validation. 9. Keep cloud DTOs separate
from Room entities where appropriate; use explicit mapping. 10. Validate
input on client and rules/server side where supported. Client-side
validation alone is not a security boundary. 11. Do not upload device
contacts automatically. Only app-created/selected contacts are synced.
12. Do not sync vault files by default without a user-visible setting
and explicit action. 13. Show last sync time, sync-in-progress status,
offline state, and actionable errors. 14. Implement retry with bounded
exponential backoff for transient failures. 15. Avoid unbounded
listeners, duplicate listeners, or per-item listener explosion. 16. Use
pagination/queries where appropriate for larger lists. 17. Respect
Firebase quotas and avoid downloading the entire database on every
launch. 18. Do not put personal data in analytics or crash-report logs.
19. Use a stable per-user path layout and document it in
docs/FIREBASE_SETUP.md. 20. Handle sign-out without accidentally
exposing the previous user’s cached data to the next account. Clear or
partition user-scoped local data safely.

SUGGESTED REALTIME DATABASE TREE users/ {uid}/ profile/ contacts/
{contactId}/ notes/ {noteId}/ tasks/ {taskId}/ transactions/
{transactionId}/ budgets/ {budgetId}/ habits/ {habitId}/
habitCompletions/ {completionId}/ goals/ {goalId}/ quickAccess/
{itemId}/ syncMetadata/ Use this only as a starting point. Avoid placing
large binary data in Realtime Database. Store images/files in Storage
and put only metadata/object paths in RTDB.

SYNC DESIGN - Local write first: save to Room immediately and mark
pending. - UI updates from Room Flow immediately. - Sync worker/listener
pushes pending mutations and applies remote changes to Room. - Use
stable IDs and idempotent operations. - Prevent infinite loops where
applying a remote change triggers another upload. - Use tombstones for
deletions until confirmed synced. - Handle simultaneous edits with a
documented deterministic conflict strategy, e.g. server
timestamp/version and last-write-wins with a conflict notice for
important fields. Do not silently lose edits without defined behavior. -
Preserve createdAt and update updatedAt consistently. - Store server
timestamps when appropriate, but handle offline local timestamps. - When
connectivity returns, reconcile pending operations in deterministic
order. - If a sync operation fails, keep the local record and show
pending/error status. - If auth expires, preserve local data and request
sign-in without destructive clearing. - Never block normal local CRUD on
cloud availability. - Add a “Sync now” action and “Pause sync”
preference if appropriate. - Document how the user can disable cloud
sync and what happens to already-uploaded data.

========================================================================================
G. CONTACTS DIRECTORY — DETAILED IMPLEMENTATION
========================================================================================
This module is a top-priority requirement. Implement real persistent
CRUD, not sample cards.

CONTACT LIST SCREEN - Screen title “Contacts”. - Search field searches
name, nickname, email, phone, company, tags, and address where
practical. - Search must be case-insensitive and accent-tolerant where
possible. - Sort options: name A–Z, recently updated, recently added,
favorites first. - Filters: favorites, tags, recently added. - Group
alphabetically if the UX remains smooth; do not make the list hard to
scan. - Floating/toolbar Add Contact action. - Empty state with “Add
your first contact”. - Show avatar or initials, name, one useful
secondary field, favorite indicator, and sync status where relevant. -
Avoid showing too much private data in notification previews or app
switcher snapshots.

ADD / EDIT CONTACT SCREEN - Name required. - Email optional and
validated only when supplied. - Phone optional; support multiple phone
numbers with labels. - Image optional: use Android Photo Picker; copy
into app-managed storage when needed for durable local use. - Address
fields optional; provide a “Copy address” action and optional
open-in-maps action. - Company and job title optional. -
Birthday/important date optional. Do not request calendar permissions
unless the user enables calendar integration. - Tags and personal notes
optional. - Save, cancel, delete, favorite, and pin actions. - Show
validation messages next to fields. - Preserve input on recoverable
errors. - Confirm deletion and explain whether the record will be
removed from synced devices/cloud. - Avoid accidental loss when
navigating away from a dirty form. - Provide a way to clear the photo
and remove optional values. - Support long names, Unicode, Bangla,
Armenian, English, accented characters, and right-to-left layout where
supported. - Avoid storing whitespace-only names.

CONTACT DETAIL SCREEN - Display the profile image/avatar, name,
company/title, and organized sections for phone, email, address,
important dates, tags, and notes. - Each optional section should be
hidden when empty or display a clear “not added” state without
clutter. - Tap phone to open dialer with ACTION_DIAL by default; do not
place calls directly. - Tap email to open an email app using
ACTION_SENDTO/mailto when available. - Tap address to open a maps intent
with properly encoded query. - Copy individual values and provide safe
feedback. - Share contact only when the user explicitly presses Share;
use Android Sharesheet and include only selected fields. - Favorite/pin
toggle must persist. - Edit and Delete actions. - Search results should
navigate to the correct contact detail. - Handle missing/removed photos
gracefully. - Use content descriptions for photo and icon actions.

CONTACT IMPORT / EXPORT - No silent bulk collection of device
contacts. - Offer optional “Import from device contacts” only after user
action; use system picker where possible and request only necessary
permission. - Preview selected contact before importing. - Avoid
duplicates using normalized phone/email heuristics, but ask before
merging. - Optional export to JSON/CSV/vCard only through explicit user
action. - Export must warn that exported files may be unencrypted and
should be stored carefully. - Do not export passwords, vault secrets,
encryption keys, auth tokens, or hidden internal metadata. - Add an
optional encrypted backup/export format for private app data if
feasible; use a well-designed authenticated encryption scheme and a
user-provided passphrase with a safe key-derivation function, not a
hard-coded key. - Do not promise recovery if the user loses both the
device and the backup/passphrase.

========================================================================================
H. MODULE 1 — HOME DASHBOARD
======================================================================================== -
Create a responsive dashboard showing greeting/date, quick actions,
today’s tasks, pinned notes, upcoming reminders, recent contacts, and a
small money summary. - Allow the user to choose which cards appear and
their order, persisted in DataStore or Room as appropriate. - Quick
actions: Add Contact, Add Note, Add Task, Add Transaction, Add Vault
Item. - Dashboard cards must read from repository/ViewModel state, not
hard-coded sample values. - Use real counts and recent items from local
database. - Clicking a card opens the correct screen or filtered list. -
Include a privacy-conscious app-switcher view; optionally obscure
sensitive dashboard details when the app is backgrounded if biometric
lock is enabled. - Empty dashboard should guide the user to create
records without looking broken. - Do not fabricate transactions or
contacts in production mode. - Provide optional demo data only when
explicitly enabled by the user. - Refresh should be driven by Flow and
sync events, not repeated full database reads. - Avoid expensive
recomposition and nested scrolling problems.

========================================================================================
I. MODULE 2 — NOTES AND JOURNAL
======================================================================================== -
Create, read, update, delete notes. - Support title, body, category,
tags, pin/favorite, created/updated time. - Support journal entries with
entry date, mood optional, and private body. - Search title/body; filter
by category/favorites/pinned/date. - Sort by updated date or created
date. - Autosave or explicit save with robust unsaved-change handling.
Choose one clear model and communicate it in UI. - For autosave,
debounce writes and flush on lifecycle transitions without losing
content. - For explicit save, warn on exit when unsaved edits exist. -
Use multiline text fields with proper scrolling and keyboard handling. -
Add note character/size limits to prevent abusive or accidental huge
records; document limits. - Do not put note body in logs, analytics,
notifications, or crash reports. - Optional Markdown preview only if
implemented safely; never render untrusted content as executable HTML. -
Offline edits must be saved locally and queued for sync. - Conflict
handling must be consistent with the sync strategy. - Deleting a note
requires confirmation or a recoverable trash mechanism. - Provide undo
for accidental deletion if feasible.

========================================================================================
J. MODULE 3 — TASKS AND REMINDERS
======================================================================================== -
Create/edit/delete tasks with title, description, due date, reminder,
priority, status, optional category/tags, and recurrence. - Statuses:
TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, CANCELLED or a simpler documented equivalent. -
Views: Today, Upcoming, All, Completed. - Filters: priority, status,
date, category. - Sort by due date, priority, created date. - Allow
completing a task from list/detail and persist immediately. - Reminders
must use notification channels, clear title/body, correct tap
destination, and unique PendingIntent identities. - Ask for notification
permission on Android versions that require it at an appropriate time,
not immediately on first launch without context. - Explain when
reminders may be delayed by battery optimization or OS restrictions. -
Handle time zones and daylight-saving changes using appropriate
java.time APIs. - Re-schedule reminders after device reboot if required
and permitted. - On task edit/delete/completion, update/cancel old
reminder to prevent duplicates. - Recurrence must not create duplicate
next tasks after repeated app starts. - Exact alarms are only for
user-visible reminders that truly require precision; use fallback
scheduling when exact permission is unavailable. - Avoid requesting
full-screen intent permission. - Test notification tap, lock screen,
denied permission, reboot, offline mode, and task deletion.

========================================================================================
K. MODULE 4 — MONEY MANAGER
======================================================================================== -
Support income and expense records. - Fields: amount, currency, title,
category, date, optional payment method, note. - Categories should be
editable and seeded with sensible defaults only once; user can create
custom categories. - Show totals by currency separately. - Show
month-to-date income, expenses, net amount, category breakdown, and
transaction history. - Provide date range filtering and search. -
Provide budget per month/category/currency with progress indication. -
Warn when budget reaches configurable thresholds. - Use integer minor
units or BigDecimal; never use Double for money arithmetic. - Validate
amount > 0, currency supported by app, and date. - Format amounts using
locale-aware NumberFormat. - Changing display locale must not corrupt
stored values. - Do not silently convert between AMD, BDT, USD, or other
currencies. - If a currency has no minor unit or a different number of
minor digits, handle currency metadata correctly. - Export CSV only on
explicit request and warn about privacy. - Avoid financial advice
claims; this is a personal bookkeeping tool. - No bank credentials, card
numbers, or automatic bank scraping. - Keep transaction descriptions
private and out of logs.

========================================================================================
L. MODULE 5 — PRIVATE VAULT
======================================================================================== -
Vault stores selected personal documents, images, files, and secure
notes in app-private storage. - Use Android Photo Picker and Storage
Access Framework; avoid broad READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE /
MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE unless genuinely essential (it should not be
essential here). - Copy selected files to managed app-private storage
when durable access is needed. Validate file size and MIME type. -
Implement authenticated encryption with a vetted Android-compatible
library or platform cryptography APIs, using AES-GCM or another
appropriate authenticated-encryption scheme. - Generate and protect
encryption keys using Android Keystore where suitable. Never hard-code
keys or save them in plain preferences. - Store nonce/IV and encryption
format version alongside ciphertext; never reuse a nonce with the same
key. - Define safe key lifecycle, lock/unlock behavior, and error
handling. - A biometric prompt should unlock access to a key or vault
session according to a documented design; biometric data itself must
never be collected or stored by this app. - Use a passcode fallback only
if designed securely; never store raw PIN in plain text. Rate-limit
attempts and avoid insecure homemade cryptography. - Lock vault after
configurable inactivity/background timeout. - Hide sensitive content
from notification previews, logs, screenshots where appropriate, and
Android Recents where appropriate. Explain that screenshot blocking is
not absolute protection. - Do not upload vault contents to Firebase by
default. If cloud backup is later added, require explicit opt-in and
upload only encrypted data with a documented threat model. - Deleting a
vault item should delete ciphertext and metadata safely. Explain
limitations of secure deletion on flash storage. - Handle missing keys,
corrupted files, app reinstall, biometric enrollment changes, and lost
passphrase without falsely promising recovery. - Do not implement
password manager functionality unless secure password generation,
autofill, encryption, and threat-model work are explicitly designed.
Generic secure notes are safer for the first release.

========================================================================================
M. MODULE 6 — CALENDAR, HABITS, AND GOALS
======================================================================================== -
Provide an in-app calendar/list of upcoming personal dates, tasks,
reminders, and optional contact important dates. - Do not request
Android Calendar access unless the user enables actual calendar
integration. - Distinguish app-local events from system-calendar
events. - Habits: create/edit/archive habit, schedule days, mark
completed for a local date, view streak/history. - Streak calculation
must handle missed days, schedule days, time zones, and date changes
consistently. - Prevent duplicate completion rows for the same
habit/date. - Goals: title, description, target value, current progress,
unit, target date, status. - Validate numeric goals and progress; allow
non-numeric goals only if a clear model is designed. - Provide progress
visuals with accessible text labels. - Do not shame the user for missed
habits; use neutral language. - Dashboard widgets should update when
completion/progress changes. - Store dates in a documented way,
distinguishing date-only values from instants. - Sync offline edits
later without duplicating completion records.

========================================================================================
N. MODULE 7 — QUICK ACCESS AND PERSONAL CONTACTS
========================================================================================
QUICK ACCESS - Save URLs, phone numbers, email addresses, addresses, and
plain text snippets. - Categories, pinned shortcuts, custom order,
search, edit/delete. - Validate URL schemes; only open safe http/https
links by default. - Phone opens dialer, email opens email composer,
address opens maps, text supports copy. - Confirm before launching
unknown or potentially unsafe external schemes. - Never execute
arbitrary scripts or treat saved text as code.

PERSONAL CONTACTS - Implement the full contact requirements in section
G. - Contacts are first-class and accessible directly from the home
screen. - Support user-entered personal information with optional fields
and a rich detail view. - Contacts are app-owned records, not
automatically the phone’s entire address book. - Contact photos should
have a local managed copy and optional Firebase Storage copy when sync
is enabled. - Cloud contact records must be under the authenticated
UID. - Personal notes on contacts should be treated as sensitive; do not
include them in notification content or logs.

========================================================================================
O. SETTINGS, BACKUP, PRIVACY, AND ACCOUNT
========================================================================================
SETTINGS SCREEN - Theme: system/light/dark, dark default. - Language:
use Android resource localization, at least English; keep strings out of
hard-coded composables. Structure for future Bengali and Armenian
translations. - Default currency selection. - Reminder/notification
settings. - Biometric lock toggle and auto-lock timeout. - Sync status,
sync now, pause/resume sync. - Cloud account state and sign out. - Local
data management, export, import, backup/restore. - About page,
version/build number, privacy summary, open-source notices. - Developer
diagnostics screen should avoid private content and be disabled or
clearly separated in production.

BACKUP / RESTORE - Offer explicit export/backup and restore. - Clearly
distinguish plain export from encrypted backup. - Encrypted backup must
use authenticated encryption and a strong passphrase-based key
derivation function with salt; document algorithm parameters and format
version. - Do not upload backup files automatically. - On restore,
preview what will be imported and handle duplicates. - Never overwrite
all current data without confirmation and a recovery/backup option. -
Test corrupted backup, wrong passphrase, unsupported version, low
storage, and interrupted restore. - Cloud sync is not the same as an
independent backup. Explain this in UI/docs.

PRIVACY - No advertising SDKs, analytics, tracking, or third-party data
sharing unless explicitly requested later. - Do not request unnecessary
permissions. - Provide a concise privacy screen describing local data,
Firebase sync, storage of photos/files, and deletion behavior. - Make
cloud sync opt-in or clearly disclose it before sign-in/sync begins.
Because this build includes Firebase, the user must knowingly
enable/configure cloud sync. - Provide local-only mode when Firebase is
unconfigured or user disables sync, while explaining that cloud copies
previously uploaded must be deleted from Firebase separately or through
an implemented deletion flow. - Ensure one user’s cached records cannot
appear after another user signs in. - Do not log personal data, tokens,
note bodies, contact information, transaction descriptions, or vault
metadata beyond what is strictly necessary.

========================================================================================
P. GITHUB, LARGE FILES, AND REPOSITORY HYGIENE
======================================================================================== -
GitHub is for source code, Gradle files, documentation, tests, and
appropriately licensed small assets. - Do not use a GitHub repository as
a live database or as a replacement for Firebase Realtime Database. - Do
not commit local databases, private contact exports, photos, vault
files, keystores, signing passwords, service-account JSON, personal
secrets, or real user data. - Include a .gitignore for
Android/Gradle/IDE/build artifacts and secrets. - Use Git LFS only for
legitimate large binary assets when repository policy and licensing
permit. Consider GitHub Releases for build artifacts instead of storing
large APKs in normal Git history. - Fonts must have compatible licenses.
Keep license notices and attribution. - Use placeholder Firebase
configuration documentation; do not invent a real
google-services.json. - If google-services.json is missing, document how
to add the user’s own file and configure Gradle correctly. Keep the app
buildable in local-only mode where feasible. - Add README instructions
for clone/open/build/install and Firebase setup. - Add a release
checklist and privacy/security checklist. - Use meaningful commits if
Git is available, but never push to a remote without explicit user
authorization.

========================================================================================
Q. ERROR HANDLING, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY
======================================================================================== -
No uncaught exceptions from normal user actions. - No main-thread
database/network/file I/O. - No hard-coded sample content in production
screens. - No swallowed exceptions; map failures to safe UI messages and
log only non-sensitive technical context. - Avoid nested unbounded
listeners and duplicated flows. - Use lazy lists for large
collections. - Debounce search and cancel stale searches. - Avoid
storing bitmaps in Room; use managed file paths/Storage paths. - Handle
null/empty optional data without crashes. - Support Unicode names, long
text, and empty values. - Use stable keys in LazyColumn. - Use content
descriptions for icon-only controls. - Touch targets should be
comfortably accessible (around 48dp when practical). - Respect system
font scaling. - Do not communicate status by color alone. - Ensure
contrast in dark and light themes. - Handle process death and
configuration changes. - Use java.time for dates and time zones. -
Ensure list/detail screens refresh after CRUD operations. - Avoid
unnecessary battery use and frequent background polling. - Use Firebase
listeners or efficient queries rather than periodic full refresh. - Do
not request location access for an address field; open maps with the
saved address only after user action. - No hidden microphone, camera,
location, SMS, call, or contacts collection.

========================================================================================
R. TESTING AND ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
========================================================================================
Create unit tests and/or instrumented tests for meaningful business
logic. At minimum verify: 1. Room database opens and schema migrations
work. 2. Contact CRUD persists across process/app restart. 3. Contact
search handles Unicode and optional fields. 4. Contact validation
rejects blank names and accepts missing email/photo. 5. Multiple phone
numbers persist and display correctly. 6. Contact photo remains
available after process restart and permission changes. 7. Notes CRUD,
search, pin/favorite, and edit persistence work. 8. Task CRUD,
completion state, filters, and date handling work. 9. Reminder
scheduling does not duplicate notifications after edit/reboot/relaunch.
10. Money calculations do not use floating-point errors. 11. Different
currencies are totaled separately. 12. Budget calculations handle empty
data and date boundaries. 13. Habit completion cannot duplicate for the
same date. 14. Vault encrypt/decrypt round-trip succeeds with correct
key. 15. Vault decryption fails safely for wrong key/tampered
ciphertext. 16. Vault content is not written to logs. 17. Quick Access
validates URL schemes. 18. Offline local CRUD works when
Firebase/network is unavailable. 19. Pending sync retries after
connectivity returns. 20. Realtime updates from one signed-in session
reach another authorized session if Firebase is configured. 21.
Unauthenticated users cannot read/write protected Firebase paths. 22.
User A cannot read/write User B’s records. 23. Signing out does not
expose cached data to the next user. 24. Firebase unconfigured/local
mode does not crash. 25. Empty, loading, error, and retry states are
reachable. 26. Rotation/process recreation does not lose unsaved data
unexpectedly. 27. Large lists scroll smoothly and search stays
responsive. 28. Permission denied states provide a usable fallback. 29.
Light and dark themes both render correctly. 30. TalkBack labels and
large-font layout are usable. 31. Backup export/import round-trip
preserves supported data. 32. Corrupted/wrong-password backup fails
safely without destructive partial import. 33. Build and lint commands
are run when the environment supports them. 34. App launches on an
emulator/device if available. 35. No secrets or private test data are
committed. Do not mark any test as passed unless it was actually
executed. Add a table to TEST_PLAN.md with status: PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN
and evidence.

========================================================================================
S. BUILD, INSTALL, AND RELEASE INSTRUCTIONS
======================================================================================== -
Run Gradle sync/compile/build tasks available in the environment. - Run
unit tests and lint when available. - Fix all compile errors introduced
by the implementation. - If Android SDK/device access is available,
install and launch the app. - Do not state that the app was installed on
the user’s phone unless the user did it or the environment verified
it. - Keep applicationId stable. - Use a sensible
versionCode/versionName and document how to increment them. - Debug APK
may be generated for local installation; release signing must use the
user’s own secure signing key and must not be generated with a
hard-coded password. - Do not commit keystore files. - If APK output
path is known and the file exists, report exact path; otherwise give
Android Studio menu steps. - Provide instructions: open project root in
Android Studio, sync Gradle, configure Firebase if desired, choose
device, run app, and build APK. - Document the minimum Android SDK
choice based on current dependencies and intended devices; do not guess
incompatible values.

========================================================================================
T. FINAL DELIVERY FORMAT
========================================================================================
At completion, respond with: 1. What was implemented. 2. Actual project
structure and key files. 3. Exact features working now versus partially
implemented. 4. Firebase setup status and exact remaining user actions.
5. Build/test commands executed and actual results. 6. Known limitations
and security caveats. 7. Android Studio steps to build/install. 8. Where
the debug APK exists only if it was actually created. 9. Next-step
checklist. Never claim all seven modules are complete if any are only
placeholders. Never leave fake buttons or “coming soon” UI while
describing them as working.

possible; do not crash or swallow the error. - OFFLINE: Ensure the
feature remains usable offline to the extent supported by local data and
queue cloud mutations for later sync. - PERSISTENCE: Verify the data
survives screen navigation, process recreation, and app restart when the
feature promises persistence. - ACCESSIBILITY: Provide readable labels,
touch targets, keyboard support, screen-reader semantics, and large-font
behavior. - SECURITY: Keep private values out of logs, analytics,
notifications, exported data by default, and unauthorized cloud paths. -
TESTING: Add or update a test for the main behavior and record whether
it was actually executed.

========================================================================================
U. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER AND EXECUTION CONTRACT
========================================================================================
Follow this order, adapting to existing project conditions: 1. Workspace
inspection and report. 2. Foundation: Gradle, package, theme,
navigation, Room, DataStore, repository boundaries. 3. Implement all
data entities/DAOs/migrations and local repositories. 4. Build polished
reusable UI components and Home Dashboard. 5. Implement Contacts fully
first because it is the user’s main feature. 6. Implement Notes and
Journal. 7. Implement Tasks and Reminders. 8. Implement Money Manager
with decimal-safe arithmetic. 9. Implement Private Vault security design
and tests before exposing a UI. 10. Implement Calendar, Habits, and
Goals. 11. Implement Quick Access. 12. Implement Settings,
backup/restore, privacy screen. 13. Implement Firebase Auth, Realtime
Database, Storage, security rules, sync queue and status. 14. Add tests,
run build/lint, fix issues, update docs. 15. Review all screens for
placeholders, fake buttons, sample-only behavior, accessibility, and
errors. 16. Final delivery report with honest status.

Do not attempt to dump the entire project into a single giant source
file. Use a proper multi-file project. A large prompt is a
specification, not a reason to generate 20,000 lines of code in one
file. Prefer maintainable code and staged implementation inside the same
project.

========================================================================================
V. FIREBASE SECURITY RULES STARTING POINT (ADAPT AND TEST)
========================================================================================
Create docs with a safe rules template tailored to the chosen Realtime
Database schema. The template must deny access by default and scope each
read/write to auth.uid matching the path UID. Validate types/field sizes
where feasible. Storage rules must scope object paths to the
authenticated UID and restrict content types/size as appropriate. Do not
use: { “rules”: { “.read”: true, “.write”: true } } Do not claim a rules
file is production-safe until it has been tested against the actual
schema and user flows. Explain that Firebase Console deployment is a
user-controlled step and do not deploy anything without authorization.

========================================================================================
W. DEFINITION OF DONE
========================================================================================
The app is not done merely because it compiles or looks attractive. A
module is complete only when: - Its primary UI is implemented. - Its
data model and persistence path work. - Create/read/update/delete
actions work where relevant. - Validation and error states work. -
Offline behavior is implemented and described. - Cloud sync is
implemented or clearly marked unconfigured with a working local mode. -
Accessibility and responsive layout have been checked. - Relevant tests
exist and their real status is reported. - README and implementation
status are updated. - No fake action buttons remain. - No secrets or
private user data are included in source control.

========================================================================================
X. USER-FACING COPY AND LANGUAGE SUPPORT
======================================================================================== -
Use concise, respectful English by default; keep all UI strings in
resources. - Prepare the resource structure for Bengali and Armenian
translations without machine-translating critical privacy/security text
without review. - Error messages must explain what happened and what the
user can do next. - Confirmation dialog must clearly identify
destructive actions. - Do not use vague messages such as “Something went
wrong” when a specific safe explanation is available. - Use consistent
terminology for Contact, Note, Task, Transaction, Vault Item, Habit,
Goal, and Quick Access. - Avoid grammar mistakes and inconsistent
capitalization. - Format date/time/currency using locale-aware APIs. -
Do not expose stack traces or Firebase raw error strings to end users.

========================================================================================
Y. README AND DOCUMENTATION CONTENT
========================================================================================
README.md must include: - App purpose and core modules. - Architecture
summary. - Required software and Android Studio version constraints
discovered from project. - How to open and build. - How to run
local-only mode. - Firebase project setup steps. - How to add
google-services.json safely. - Authentication provider setup. - Realtime
Database schema overview. - Security rules setup and testing
instructions. - Firebase Storage setup. - Offline sync design and
conflict policy. - Vault encryption and recovery limitations. -
Permission explanations. - Backup/export warnings. - How to run tests. -
How to create a debug APK. - Release signing safety. - Known limitations
and future extension guide.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: - UI/data/domain boundaries. - Repository
pattern. - Room source-of-truth policy. - Firebase sync lifecycle. -
Feature module boundaries. - How to add a future feature.

docs/SECURITY.md: - Threat model. - What is stored locally/cloud. -
Encryption boundaries. - Authentication and rules. - Backup and recovery
risks. - Logging policy. - Data deletion policy.

docs/FIREBASE_SETUP.md: - Exact project setup steps. - Auth provider
enablement. - Realtime Database creation and region choice guidance. -
Storage setup. - Rules deployment steps. - Emulator testing where
possible. - Troubleshooting without revealing secrets.

docs/TEST_PLAN.md: - Test case, expected result, actual status,
evidence. - Clearly distinguish automated tests, manual tests, and NOT
RUN.

docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md: - Version bump. - Signing. - Permission
review. - Firebase rules review. - Backup and migration test. -
Install/update test. - Privacy review.
